question.text: Under the SEBI (Intermediaries) Regulations, 2008, how can a notice or order be served on a stock broker?

answer.text: By hand delivery; by registered post, speed post, courier or electronic mail to the address on SEBI records; through the concerned stock exchange or depository for brokers, sub-brokers and depository participants; or by affixing at the premises if the other methods fail
Only through the concerned stock exchange
Only by registered post, speed post, courier, or electronic mail to the address on SEBI records
Only by hand delivery to the concerned person or authorized agent

explanation.text: The Logic: A notice or order may be served by hand delivery, by registered post / speed post / courier / electronic mail or other recorded delivery to the address on SEBI's records, through the concerned stock exchange or depository (for brokers, sub-brokers and depository participants), or by affixing at the premises if the other methods fail. The Trap: Each "Only..." option names one valid mode of service, but the regulations permit several alternative methods — restricting service to one mode misstates the rule. Note: The keyed option was rewritten as a standalone comprehensive list (instead of "All of the above") so the item stays correct under answer randomization. The unsupported Cross-Exam Context and Pro-Tip paragraphs were removed.
